# Simulation and planning the number of replicates

## 1 Abstract

Simulated data with known effects show how well an analysis recovers
them, which is useful in teaching, and how often its tests detect
effects of a given size, which is the basis for planning an experiment.
[`DiallelSim()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelSim.md)
draws the data and
[`DiallelPower()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelPower.md)
estimates the power of the combining-ability tests.

## 2 Simulation and the number of replicates

[`DiallelSim()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelSim.md)
draws plot data from Griffing’s model with chosen standard deviations of
the effects and returns the true effects with the data, so the estimates
can be compared with the truth:

``` r

s <-
  DiallelSim(
      Parents = 6
    , Method  = 1
    , Rep     = 4
    , Env     = 1
    , Mean    = 100
    , gca     = 5
    , sca     = 3
    , rec     = 1
    , gcaEnv  = 0
    , scaEnv  = 0
    , EnvSD   = 0
    , Block   = 2
    , Error   = 4
    , seed    = 123
    )
fs <-
  Griffing(
      y          = y
    , Rep        = Rep
    , Cross1     = Cross1
    , Cross2     = Cross2
    , data       = s
    , Method     = 1
    , Model      = 1
    , Reciprocal = c("combined", "split")[1]
    )
round(x = cbind(true = attr(x = s, which = "truth")$gca, estimated = fs$GCA), digits = 2)
```

       true estimated
    1 -5.04     -5.01
    2 -3.39     -3.14
    3  5.56      6.09
    4 -1.88     -1.58
    5 -1.59     -2.87
    6  6.34      6.51

[`DiallelPower()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelPower.md)
repeats such simulations to estimate the power of the gca and sca tests
for several numbers of replicates, which helps to plan an experiment:

``` r

pw <-
  DiallelPower(
      Parents = 6
    , Method  = 2
    , Rep     = 2:5
    , Model   = 1
    , gca     = 1
    , sca     = 1.5
    , rec     = 0
    , Error   = 4
    , nsim    = 200
    , alpha   = 0.05
    , seed    = 1
    )
pw
```

         Rep Source Power         SE
       <int> <char> <num>      <num>
    1:     2    gca 0.320 0.03298485
    2:     2    sca 0.115 0.02255826
    3:     3    gca 0.425 0.03495533
    4:     3    sca 0.270 0.03139267
    5:     4    gca 0.605 0.03456696
    6:     4    sca 0.340 0.03349627
    7:     5    gca 0.665 0.03337477
    8:     5    sca 0.370 0.03413942

``` r

plot(x = pw)
```

## 3 Summary

[`DiallelSim()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelSim.md)
gives data with known effects for teaching and checking;
[`DiallelPower()`](https://myaseen208.com/DiallelAnalysisR/reference/DiallelPower.md)
shows how many replicates detect gca and sca effects of a given size.

## 4 References

Griffing, B. (1956). Concept of general and specific combining ability
in relation to diallel crossing systems. *Australian Journal of
Biological Sciences*, 9(4), 463–493.
